relationships.title: Review and control action while a judicial case is pending on appeal

metadata.summary: A higher court may note an exception through review and control but may take no action on it while judicial proceedings are pending; the effect of any unconstitutional act is suspended upon appeal.

relationships.title: Proper use of memorials and finality of adjudicated GA decisions

metadata.summary: A memorial under BCO 40-5 is the proper recourse for alleging GA error after adjournment; the Assembly will not reopen a finally adjudicated case except to correct a manifest error.

relationships.title: Notice of complaint sufficiency and timing of suspension motion under BCO 43-4

metadata.summary: Northeast Presbytery asked whether a written statement of intent to complain constitutes adequate notice to suspend a court's action and when a suspension motion is procedurally in order.

relationships.title: Recourse when General Assembly may have erred in a decision

metadata.summary: The CCB advised that errors alleged during a GA meeting may be challenged under BCO 45, and subsequent assemblies may take contrary positions but cannot annul prior actions.

relationships.title: Scope and duration of BCO debate prohibitions during a complaint

metadata.summary: BCO prohibitions on debate apply only to the specific matter complained, only until final adjudication, and to all members of the lower court — expiring upon final resolution.

topics: complaint out of order by lower court
metadata.synopsis: The SJC denied a minister's complaint challenging Presbytery's out-of-order dismissal of his request for a BCO 31-2 investigation of another minister. Although the SJC agreed Presbytery wrongly said it had already decided all issues—the earlier complaint (SJC 2010-28) was distinct—it upheld the refusal to investigate. The accused minister had delivered an authorized committee report as chairman; absent evidence he exceeded that authorization, his statements were the committee's, not personal, and BCO 31-2 did not require investigation.

metadata.synopsis: North Florida Presbytery restored a minister deposed for adultery by a 19–17 vote. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that Presbytery had not proceeded with the required caution and that a bare majority could not demonstrate BCO 34-8’s required strongly favorable general sentiment. It declined to require reordination, calling that question unsettled and treating BCO 37-5’s restoration pronouncement as sufficient pending clarification. The SJC annulled Presbytery’s actions concerning the minister and remanded for a proper probationary and review process.

Sherfey challenged James River Presbytery’s denial of his complaint and alleged errors in its commission’s proceedings. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order with incurable defects: several grounds had not first been adjudicated by Presbytery as BCO 43-2 required, and the General Assembly filing missed BCO 43-3’s thirty-day deadline. Incorrect advice from Presbytery’s clerk did not excuse compliance. The adopted decision neither reached the merits nor ordered a remand; only a concurrence proposed returning the matter to Presbytery.

metadata.synopsis: Southwest Florida Presbytery denied Armes's second complaint as a mere restatement of Case 2009-12; the SJC sustained the complaint and remanded, finding the second complaint involved distinct post-censure acts (the trespass notice) that could not be dismissed as identical in substance. A dissenting opinion argued Armes, as an excommunicated person, lacked standing to bring any complaint beyond the limited access afforded under BCO 38-1.

metadata.synopsis: At issue was whether James River Presbytery erred by instructing TE Andrew Conrad not to teach or preach his views that the Genesis days were not necessarily six twenty-four-hour days, after JRP treated the views as an exception. The SJC denied the complaint, leaving JRP's instruction in effect. It deferred under BCO 39-3, finding no significant procedural or constitutional error and no clear error of discretion; the parties had stipulated that instruction as the sole issue. The eight dissenters would have found JRP exceeded its discretion.

relationships.title: Nickoley and Stephens v. Southwest Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: Complainants challenged Southwest Presbytery's January 1991 actions: withdrawing charges against two ruling elders, dissolving Pastor Pollock's pastoral relationship, and rescinding its suspension of Covenant PC's session. The SJC did not sustain the complaint and affirmed. It held the BCO gives no presbytery authority to suspend a session or act as a Session pro tem without formal congregational consent; BCO 31-1 left the elder charges with the session, so they were never validly before Presbytery; the dissolution challenge was moot after Pollock left the PCA, though Presbytery acted correctly on the congregation's request.
